title: Active Directory: The Heart of Windows Server

scenes.line1: What's the backbone of Windows domains?
scenes.say: Ever wonder what really holds a Windows domain together? Let's break down why Active Directory is the core of everything.

scenes.label: DC
scenes.sub: Domain controllers authenticate users and replicate changes.
scenes.say: Domain controllers are the servers that handle logins and keep the directory in sync across your network.
When a user logs in, their computer finds a domain controller through DNS. The controller checks their credentials, applies group policy, and any changes get copied to other controllers.
Remember, an organizational unit is for organizing and linking group policies, while a security group is for giving permissions.

scenes.title: PowerShell: Your AD Swiss Army Knife
scenes.say: PowerShell is the admin's Swiss Army knife. You can search users, check group members, and create accounts all from the command line.

scenes.question: What breaks if DNS fails in AD?
scenes.right: Domain logins and finding controllers fail too.
scenes.say: Here's a classic trap: if DNS breaks, it's not just names that stop working. Clients can't find domain controllers, so logins and group policy fail as well.
